description: v2.0 Phase 1 (C1.5) — 40-task eval suite. 28 fast + 12 hard. Hard tasks are where DSPy (Phase 3) gets a real gradient to optimize against; if all 40 pass on a stock orchestrator prompt, DSPy has no signal. We deliberately bias the hard tasks toward situations the supervisor commonly mishandles (concurrency edge cases, distributed semantics, multi-file consistency, opinionated writing).

tasks.task: Build a Python CLI calculator at calc.py with no external dependencies. Supports + - * / and parentheses.
list 5 best mango varieties grown in India with their region and season
build a hello world android app in kotlin with min sdk 24, XML views
Compare Postgres vs SQLite for a 1k-user webapp. Output postgres_vs_sqlite.md.
draft a 1-page product spec for a habit tracker app
list 5 popular gradually-typed languages with one-line strengths
Write a 250-word launch blog announcing a new file-share product called Folio. Tone: confident, plain English.
Draft an incident postmortem for a 47-min outage caused by a runaway DB migration. Include timeline, root cause, mitigations.
Convert this CSV (3 cols: name, region, score) into a sorted markdown table by score desc. Source data: alice,IN,87 / bob,US,92 / carlos,BR,78. Output table.md.
Write extract_emails.py — given a string, return all email addresses (RFC-5322-loose). Include a __main__ self-test that prints results for one sample.
Produce a cron entry that runs /usr/local/bin/healthcheck.sh every 5 minutes, redirects stdout+stderr to /var/log/healthcheck.log, and a one-line README explaining it. Output cron.txt and README.md.
Write a systemd .service file for a Python web service at /opt/myapp/server.py running as user 'myapp'. Restart=on-failure. Output myapp.service and a one-paragraph install note.
Create greet.py with a function `greet(name)` that returns 'Hello, <name>'. Trivial — single file, ~5 lines.
Write fizzbuzz.py that prints 1..30 with Fizz/Buzz/FizzBuzz rules. Stdlib only. Run it and show its output in the action log.
Write anagrams.py with `is_anagram(a, b) -> bool` and a __main__ self-test for ('listen','silent') -> True and ('hello','world') -> False. Output must show both test results in the action log.
Read /etc/hostname and /etc/os-release if available, write a one-paragraph host_summary.md describing the host. Use a tiny POSIX shell script summary.sh that produces the markdown.
Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, and fixed-window rate limiting in 1 paragraph each. Output rate_limits.md.

Build a Flask REST API at app.py with endpoints GET /items, POST /items, GET /items/<id>, DELETE /items/<id>. In-memory store. Include a tests.py with at least 2 happy-path tests using Flask's test_client. Run the tests and show output.

Create a release plan for shipping a service: STEP build (compile artifact), STEP lint (run linter), STEP test (run unit tests), STEP package (create tar.gz), STEP deploy (write a deploy.sh that copies tar.gz to remote). build/lint can run in parallel; test depends on build; package depends on lint+test; deploy depends on package. Each step is a real script the next step depends on. Use the Steps section of the brief if your supervisor supports parallel execution.

Build an ELT pipeline scaffold. STEP extract (fetch.py reads a sample CSV), STEP transform (transform.py normalizes columns), STEP load (load.py writes JSON). transform depends on extract; load depends on transform. Include a runner.sh that runs all three in order. Run it once and show output.

Build todo.py — a CLI that supports `add <text>`, `list`, `done <id>`, `rm <id>`. Persist to ~/.todo.json. Stdlib only. Include __main__ self-test that adds 2 items, marks one done, lists, removes one.

Implement memoize.py with a `@memoize(ttl_secs=N, max_size=M)` decorator. LRU eviction past max_size, expiry past ttl. Include test that proves: cache hits skip the wrapped function, expiry refreshes, LRU evicts the right entry.

Compare Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, and pgvector across these axes: hosted/self-host, pricing, max vector dim, hybrid search support, license. Output vector_dbs.md as a table + 2-paragraph recommendation for a 1M-vector personal project.
Compare per-1M-token pricing (input/output) for Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5, Gemini 2 Pro, and DeepSeek V3 as of Jan 2026. Note context window for each. Output llm_pricing.md.

Write validate_users.py that loads users.json (you generate 3 sample records, 1 invalid) and validates each against a JSON Schema (name: required str, age: required int 0-150, email: required string with @). Print pass/fail per record. Stdlib only — no jsonschema dependency.

Write dedup.py that reads sample.csv (cols: name, email, score), deduplicates rows by (name, email) keeping the highest score, writes deduped.csv sorted by score desc. Generate a 5-row sample with 2 duplicates as part of the task. Show before+after row counts in the log.

Write docker-compose.yml for a stack: Postgres 16 + Redis 7 + a Python 3.12 app (you don't need to write the app, just point to a Dockerfile that doesn't have to exist). Each service must have a healthcheck. Persist Postgres data with a named volume. Include a one-page README.md explaining how to start/stop/inspect.

Write nginx.conf for an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of localhost:8000. Must include: listen 443 with SSL, proxy_pass to upstream, gzip, rate_limit zone (10r/s per IP), security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, CSP basic). Plus a NOTES.md explaining the rate-limit choice.

Write a 200-word press release announcing a fintech mobile app launch called 'Bridge'. App lets freelancers in India send/receive USD in their domestic accounts. Tone: professional, dateline format, includes one quote from CEO. Output press.md.

Write a 500-word design doc for a token-bucket rate limiter. Include: problem, design, alternatives considered (leaky bucket, fixed window), failure modes, monitoring/metrics, rollout plan. Output design.md.

Write a postmortem for a memory leak caused by an unbounded LRU cache in production. Include timeline (3 events), root cause analysis, immediate fix, longer-term prevention (e.g. cache_max_size cap, monitor RSS). 400 words max. Output postmortem.md.

Build app.py — a FastAPI service with /items CRUD backed by SQLite (sqlite3 stdlib). Endpoints: POST /items, GET /items, GET /items/{id}, PUT /items/{id}, DELETE /items/{id}. Include tests.py using FastAPI TestClient that exercises all 5 endpoints. Run tests and show output.

Implement async_rate_limit.py — an asyncio leaky-bucket rate limiter that allows max N requests per second. The bucket leaks evenly (no thundering herd at second boundaries). Include test_rate_limit.py that fires 50 concurrent callers at a 10/s limiter and asserts the 50th completes in roughly 5s, NOT all in second 1. Run the test and show timing output. The hard part: prove evenness, not just count.

Implement dijkstra.py — Dijkstra's shortest path on a weighted directed graph. Use a heap-based priority queue. Include test_dijkstra.py with 3 cases: (1) classic 5-node graph with known shortest path, (2) disconnected graph (returns inf), (3) graph with multiple equal-cost paths (any one is valid). Performance assertion: 1000-node random graph completes in under 1 second.

Write stream_agg.py that processes a 100MB CSV (you generate it: 1M rows, cols=user_id,country,amount). Aggregate total amount per country. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: peak memory usage must be < 50MB (verifiable with resource.getrusage or psutil if installed). Output result.json sorted by total desc. Show before/after memory in the action log.

Implement pg_lock.py — a distributed mutex using Postgres advisory locks (pg_advisory_lock / pg_advisory_unlock). API: `with PGLock('my_resource', dsn=...) as lock:`. Auto-releases on connection drop. Include test_pg_lock.py that spawns 2 processes contending for the same lock and proves only ONE holds it at a time. Use sqlite + a software shim if Postgres isn't available so the test still runs.

Write postgres_vs_mongo_1m.md — a deep tradeoff analysis for choosing between Postgres and MongoDB for a 1M-user social app with feed, comments, and search. Be CONCRETE not generic: include actual replication strategies, sharding implications at this scale, query latency expectations (p50/p99), operational cost estimates, and 'when would I switch?'. Length: 1200-1800 words. Filler-heavy answers will fail review.

clarifications.hard_constraint: concrete numbers + scale-specific reasoning, not generic

tasks.task: Write adr-001-message-queue.md — an Architecture Decision Record choosing between AWS SQS, Kafka, and RabbitMQ for an order-processing system. Format: Status / Context / Decision / Consequences / 'What would change my mind' (this last section is mandatory and the hard part — no generic 'we'd reconsider'). 800-1200 words.

Build server.py + my-service.service. The Python service must (1) accept SIGTERM and gracefully drain in-flight HTTP requests over 30 seconds, (2) reject NEW requests during drain (return 503), (3) exit cleanly when drain completes OR after a 35s hard timeout. systemd unit must use TimeoutStopSec=40, KillSignal=SIGTERM, Restart=on-failure. Include test_drain.py that starts the server, fires 5 long requests, sends SIGTERM mid-flight, and verifies all 5 complete + new requests are rejected. Run the test.

Implement ringbuf.py — a thread-safe bounded circular buffer with put_nowait / get_nowait / put / get. Backpressure: full buffer blocks producers; empty buffer blocks consumers. Include test_ringbuf.py with TWO scenarios: (1) 10 producers + 10 consumers + buffer-of-100 all running concurrently for 10000 messages each, no message lost or duplicated. (2) Single consumer dies mid-stream — producers eventually block but don't deadlock once a new consumer starts. Use threading + Lock + Condition; no asyncio. Run both tests.

clarifications.hard_constraint: no message lost/duplicated under concurrency; no deadlock on consumer death
